lines: adonné à toute eſpece de larrecins, & af-
Les teſmoins raportoyent qu'iceluy du Tilh eſtoit
couſtumier iurer teſte, corps, ſang & playes de noſtre
Seigneur: ce que vulgairement on appelle Blaſphemer:
qui n'eſt autre choſe, ſelon l'expoſition des Theologiẽs,
choſes à Dieu, qui ne luy conuiennent point: ou bien
detraire de ce que luy appartient {a}. combien qu'à la ve
rité, Blaſpheme ſe doyue diffinir autrement: car laiſſant
à part l'interpretation des Hebrieux, & Cabaliſtes, qui
diſent Blaſphemer le nom de Dieu n'eſtre autre choſe,
qu'exprimer ce grand & ineffable nom, Tetragramma
ton (qui ne ſe doit pronõcer ou eſcrire) Par ces lettres,
& caracteres faut entendre que Blaſpheme, eſt vn nom
tiré du Grec, qui ſignifie deteſtation, iniure, meſpris, ma
ledicẽce, & vitupere. Dont Blaſphemer, à parler propre
ment, eſt meſpriſer, deteſter, & contumelier Dieu, ou
ſon fils Ieſus Chriſt {b}, les prouoquant d'opprobres &
iniures {c}. Ainſi quãd les Iuifs iettoient des pierres cõtre
noſtre Sauuenr Ieſus-chriſt, ils diſoiẽt le lapider, nõ pas
pour bonnes œuures (comme le Seigneur iuſtemẽt ſe
plaignoit:) mais pour Blaſpheme {d}. Et tels Blaſphema-
teurs, par la loy anciéne eſtoient lapidez du peuple {e} de
laquelle nos cõſtitutiõs ciuiles eſpuiſées, condẽnent les
Blaſphemateurs à mort: ce que deuroit eſtre religieu-
ſement gardé: & (cõme dit ſainct Gregoire) ſans vier de
miſericorde aucune {f}: pourueu toutesfois qu'ils ſoient
couſtumiers & endurcis à ce faire {g}. Autremẽt pour vne,
deux & trois fois, la loy ne les fait pas mourir (ne voulãt
tirer à peine de mort trop facilemeot vn gliſſement, &
lubricité de langage {h}:) mais les puniſt extraordinaire-
mẽt, ſelon la qualité des perſonnes, & autres circonſtan
ces obſeruées: le tout remis à l'arbitre du iuge {i}: d'autãt
que la loy pẽſe, tels blaſphemes inaccouſtumez, proce-
der plus de quelque paſſion, legereté d'eſprit, ou mau

uncertain.note: the sort after d' is a blotted small glyph matching no clear letter (far smaller than the italic capital A of 'Aut,'); the final 'a' is also heavily inked but readable. With the next line 'nie' the name is probably 'Iean d'Ananie' (Ioannes de Anania, cited with 'de maled.'); the blotted sort is presumably an A. Pointer: margin-2.jpg, first line of note a, y~240.
'fina.' as printed (f-i-n-a plus point), probably an abbreviation of 'au final'; not expanded.
sic: the second letter is an open c (wrong sort for 'Tomas'), checked at 6x.
sic: a plain italic a stands where 'queſtion' needs e (no æ ligature; the glyph matches the a of 'ſa' on the line above), checked at 6x.

key layout: three consecutive margin lines open with a single lowercase italic letter at the key column ('b Aut, alearũ', 'c de religioſ', 'c leuitique.'). Both c's are the same italic sort as the text c of 'c. xxiiij.' and 'c xiiij.' below; nothing typographic separates a key c from a text c here. Resolved by sense: 'Aut, alearũ' (the Authentica 'Alearum') needs the Codex title 'C. de religioſ.' to complete the citation, so that line continues note b, and 'leuitique. / c. xxiiij.' (Leviticus 24, the stoning of the blasphemer) is note c, which is what marker {c} wants. If the compositor meant the reverse, note b is one line and note c three. Pointer: margin-2.jpg, last three lines.

the letter between the points is a closed italic e (eye and bar visible at 6x), not the open c of 'c. xxiiij.' and 'c xiiij.'; the sense wants 'c.' (chapitre) for John 10; transcribed as printed, sic.
printed 'xiiij' (14) although the passage and note c point to Leviticus 24; transcribed as printed, sic.

the word-break sign after 'ſan' prints as a raised round dot at x-height, exactly like the hyphen sorts of 'Blaſphema-' and 'religieu-' in the body of this page; transcribed as a hyphen per conventions.
three minims after the space (i, i, j with descender) at 6x; the first sort of the numeral is an open c, not x; the expected citation is C. xxiij. q. v.; transcribed as printed, sic.
the letter before o has a small closed bowl at the foot of the stem (italic b, as in 'ſoubz' below), unlike the open-legged h key of note h; read 'bo.' at 12x.
the mark between 'iiij' and 'collat.' is a short raised stroke like the line-end hyphens of this italic; transcribed as a hyphen, may be a high-set period.

the last sort before the point is an x-height u-shaped glyph with a short slanted accent stroke above it; it is not the tall ſt ligature that 'maieſt.' (ad legem Iuliam maiestatis) needs (compare 'poſtulante' in note i). Read as printed, ù; probably a damaged or wrong sort. Pointer: margin-4.jpg, second line, y~90.

no key letter is printed before this note: only a tiny round dot at mid x-height stands in the key column at 8x, which is not a legible i sort. Key left null. By elimination this note belongs to marker {i} (body line 'ces obſeruées: le tout remis à l'arbitre du iuge {i}: d'autãt'), the only marker on the page without a note, the alphabet running a-i; the note is printed four lines above the marker line because the margin leading is tighter. Pointer: margin-4.jpg, y~160, key column.
